cells.tense: You are placing your weight deliberately, and the thing is level underneath you.
cells.ask: Before the day ends, sit with one person who shares the load and say which part of it each of you is carrying — then stop and let their version stand beside yours.
cells.core:
You notice when one side of a deal has quietly gotten heavier, and you move to level it. Not later, not loudly. People hand you the thing that needs holding up, because it comes back whole. This is strength in the plain sense — a wall that was built to carry the roof. It doesn't announce itself. It just holds.

That holding is doing quiet work in more places than you'd count if you stopped to count. You probably haven't. Nobody hands out credit for things that don't tip.

So you get to choose what this feeds next. You don't have to keep it as a private lining to other people's arrangements. The offer is to let it name something forward.

cells.verb: building what holds, and recalculating when the weight shifts

cells.tense: You are already bracing against the weight that will land next, reading ahead for who will try to bend the terms.
cells.ask: For one week, keep a small tally of things you do that you didn't have to do, and beside each write whose weight it was. If the line says 'no one else's,' that one gets dropped by week's end.
cells.core:
You can see an imbalance coming before it arrives, and you're already adjusting for it. The effort is real, and it's being spent on a ledger nobody has opened. The grip tightens the more certain you get. Balance doesn't usually need holding down. A fair call made ahead of the evidence isn't justice — it's a fence built before you know which way the road runs.

Fairness doesn't take that much arithmetic. The clear sense of what's right is still under there, somewhere below the leaning. Give the next thing you weigh one look, ask if it's actually yours to carry, and if it isn't, hand it back.

cells.tense: The scale is sitting where it landed, and you have been leaving it there for some time.
cells.ask: Pick one small thing you've been sitting on and finish it today, exactly as it is, no improvements — a reply, an invoice, the last load of laundry. When it's done, notice you don't have to do anything else with it.
cells.core:
The scale is there and you've stopped picking it up. Things that aren't level sit in plain sight and no move gets made. Strength isn't the issue. What's quiet is the part that says a disagreement can be settled because both of you would still be standing afterward.

Meanwhile the work piles up. Not because you can't carry it — because you're still waiting on a verdict you aren't going to get.

A fair exchange is still possible. Settling a bill doesn't unmake anything. You're not turning your back on what happened. There's just no more standing at a door for a knock that isn't coming.
cells.sheetLine: You've stopped settling accounts because you stopped trusting the scale.

cells.tense: The adjusting is already happening here, and you're telling it as something the situation is doing to you.
cells.ask: When you catch yourself saying 'it kept going' or 'that got sorted,' stop for five seconds and finish the sentence as 'I set it.' Then notice whether the story needs to change at all, or just the one word.
cells.core:
You're already evening things out, often in the same room, without a word about it. The meeting that stays quieter once you're in it. The household that keeps not tipping. You hear yourself describing that as how things have gone.

The work is real and it's well done. What's left out is who did it. Nothing has to change in what you do — only in the telling. You are the one making the calls.

There's no need to defend it or explain how long you've been doing it. Just let the one who made the decision be named out loud when the account of how things went comes around again.
